entries.title: When Do Larger Batches Help Scale LLM Reinforcement Learning?
entries.desc: Larger batches expose more parallelism by processing more sequences per update, but under a fixed sample budget, they also leave fewer opportunities to update the model. When does this trade-off reduce wall-clock time-to-target in reinforcement learning? For large language models, answering this question requires accounting for the online generation of training trajectories and the computational asymmetry between generation and training. We develop a framework that connects samples-to-target with end-to-end throughput: a larger batch accelerates training only when its throughput gain exceeds its samples-to-target penalty. This framework also suggests a simple practical strategy—first establish approximate batch-size invariance, then optimize throughput within that regime. Experiments with GRPO and PPO show that learning-rate retuning approximately preserves sample-indexed learning trajectories over a bounded batch range. On fixed hardware, larger batches improve generation throughput by up to 2.29x, and our best measured GRPO configuration reaches the same validation target in 29% less time without additional GPUs.

entries.title: From LR to ELR: A Better Heuristic for Pretraining Dynamics
entries.desc: Understanding pretraining dynamics is crucial for designing effective training hyperparameters for large language models (LLMs), particularly the learning rate (LR). However, LR does not always reflect how much the function represented by the model actually changes, and the optimal LR often shifts with model and data scale. In this post, we identify that the effective learning rate (ELR), which controls the directional changes of model weights, is a more intrinsic heuristic than LR as a tunable hyperparameter. Specifically, ELR delivers more accurate loss prediction under the multi-power law (MPL) model and transfers more reliably across model scales. More broadly, the ELR perspective guides the design of better schedules, which outperform conventional LR-schedule baselines.

entries.title: Hyra: A simple yet effective scaffold for general discovery
entries.desc: Today, we are introducing Hyra-1.0, the first release of Hyra (Hunyuan Research Agent) - an agent capable of recursive self-improvement, purpose-built for performance-driven research and engineering tasks.

entries.title: Real life is where context gets hard
entries.desc: Previously, we built CL-Bench to test whether AI could learn complex new knowledge, such as rules, and use it effectively. But real life doesn't come with a rulebook. To be a helpful everyday assistant, an AI must do more than just understand complex rules; it should also understand complex human relationships and piece together clues from messy, scattered context.
